references.text: Tells of Esau marrying Hittite women, which was a source of grief to Isaac and Rebekah.
Rebekah expresses her displeasure with the Hittite women and does not want Jacob to marry one of the daughters of Canaan.
Isaac commands Jacob not to take a wife from the daughters of Canaan but to go to Paddan-Aram—this is what Esau observes.
Esau sees that Isaac blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-Aram to find a wife there, and that Jacob obeyed his parents.
Lists Esau's Canaanite wives, showing his choice of spouses from Canaan.
Direct narrative follow-up: Gen 28:8 shows Esau's insight into his marriage choices immediately after the conflict peak in Gen 27:41 (threat of murder) occurred.
